note: parlez français means 'speak French'; it does not explicitly express ability with pouvoir.
proposed_target: Je suppose que vous parlez français.

note: Natural direct English equivalent of ne peux rien faire is 'can't do anything', not the marked 'can do nothing'.
proposed_target: Je ne peux rien faire pour aider.
proposed_english: I can't do anything to help.

note: J'y arriverai is future and means 'I'll manage/succeed', not present 'I can do without'.
Ça va être dur d'attendre means waiting will be difficult; 'I can hardly wait' idiomatically suggests eagerness and changes meaning.
proposed_target: Ça va être dur d'attendre jusqu'à demain.
proposed_english: It will be hard to wait until tomorrow.

note: French explicitly has t'aider ('help you'); English omits the object.
proposed_target: Je peux t'aider si tu veux.
proposed_english: I can help you if you want.

note: French contains no equivalent of English 'here'.
bien adds the sense of not really/not quite knowing what to say.
proposed_target: Je ne savais pas bien quoi dire.
proposed_english: I didn't quite know what to say.

note: avait fait is pluperfect; preserve the prior-past relation in English.
proposed_target: Je ne savais pas qui avait fait ça.
proposed_english: I didn't know who had done that.

note: savais cuisiner directly means 'knew how to cook'; English 'could cook' is possible but less exact for instruction.
proposed_target: Je ne savais pas que tu savais cuisiner.
proposed_english: I didn't know you knew how to cook.

note: Present progressive is the natural English equivalent in this context; 'what you do' suggests habitual action.
proposed_target: Je ne sais pas ce que tu fais.
proposed_english: I don't know what you're doing.
